_comment: Committed app-flash and static-DRAM ceilings (bytes) per board, measured on the runner's pinned ESP-IDF (see .esp-idf-version). flash_bytes is the UNPADDED app flash footprint (flash_code + flash_rodata + flash_other from idf.py size), not the bramble.bin image: the image is padded up to 64 KiB ESP32-S3 MMU pages, so its size jumps a whole page at a boundary and can differ by 64 KiB between ESP-IDF patch versions, which is not a precise regression signal (partition fit is already enforced by the ESP-IDF build). CI fails a board when app flash or static DRAM (data + bss) grows more than tolerance_bytes above the ceiling. This file NEVER auto-drifts: a developer updates it deliberately with scripts/ci/update-size-baseline.sh (run under the CI toolchain via scripts/ci-source-idf.sh) when a change legitimately grows the binary, with the reason in the PR. tolerance_bytes (8 KiB) absorbs run-to-run and minor toolchain noise while still catching the tens-of-KiB regressions this gate exists to stop.
